Beach Point Capital Management LP Position in Xpo Logistics (XPO) Lifted as Stock Rose; Apple (AAPL) Shareholder Capital City Trust Company Has Trimmed Its Position 
April 23, 2018 - By Marguerite Chambers 
Carl Goldsmith increased its stake in Xpo Logistics Inc (XPO) by 24.35% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Beach Point Capital Management Lp bought 14,000 shares as the company’s stock rose 9.61% while stock markets declined. The hedge fund run by Carl Goldsmith held 71,500 shares of the consumer services company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $6.55M, up from 57,500 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Beach Point Capital Management Lp who had been investing in Xpo Logistics Inc for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $12.50 billion market cap company. The stock decreased 0.19% or $0.2 during the last trading session, reaching $104.24. About 572,734 shares traded. XPO Logistics, Inc. (NYSE:XPO) has risen 113.78% since April 23, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 102.23% the S&P500. 
Capital City Trust Company decreased its stake in Apple Inc (AAPL) by 6.89% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Capital City Trust Company sold 2,588 shares as the company’s stock declined 3.81% with the market. The institutional investor held 34,953 shares of the computer manufacturing company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $5.92M, down from 37,541 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Capital City Trust Company who had been investing in Apple Inc for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $837.57B market cap company. The stock decreased 0.39% or $0.65 during the last trading session, reaching $165.07. About 22.94 million shares traded. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has risen 19.49% since April 23, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 7.94% the S&P500. 
Analysts await Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) to report earnings on May, 1 after the close. They expect $2.71 earnings per share, up 29.05% or $0.61 from last year’s $2.1 per share. AAPL’s profit will be $13.75 billion for 15.23 P/E if the $2.71 EPS becomes a reality.
